extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students researching Tobias Wolff or American literature
extracted.subtask_description: An Encyclopaedia Britannica author biography summarizing Tobias Wolff's life, major works, themes, genres, and honors. Useful for readers seeking an overview of his career and the characteristics of his writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skillful depiction of many voices and a wide range of emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: “primarily known for his memoirs and for his short stories, in which many voices and a wide range of emotions are skillfully depicted.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This opening characterization identifies a quality to look for in Wolff's work: plurality of narrative voices and emotional breadth handled with craft. Use this as an evaluative lens when assessing his short stories and memoirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autobiographical focus and candid treatment of difficult family history
rubrics_metrics.description: “Wolff wrote about his childhood in the 1950s, including his relationship with his abusive stepfather, in This Boy’s Life: A Memoir.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography highlights candid, autobiographical exploration of childhood and abusive family dynamics as a defining feature; authenticity and willingness to confront personal pain are implied qualities of his memoir writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal military experience as material
rubrics_metrics.description: “Wolff served in the military as a paratrooper during the Vietnam War... Later works by Wolff include the memoir In Pharaoh’s Army: Memories of a Lost War... and The Night in Question... many of which again reflect Wolff’s time in Vietnam.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wolff draws on his Vietnam service in both memoir and fiction; fidelity to lived experience and the translation of those experiences into thematic and narrative material is a notable criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penetrating insight into moral consequences and character
rubrics_metrics.description: “The novel Old School (2003) is a penetrating look at what happens when a prep-school student plagiarizes someone else’s work in an attempt to win a literary competition.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'penetrating look' signals depth of psychological and moral insight as a measure of the novel's success—evaluate how deeply the work probes motives, consequences, and ethical complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility across forms (memoir, short story collections, novel, anthology editing)
rubrics_metrics.description: References to Wolff’s published collections (In the Garden of the North American Martyrs; Back in the World), memoirs (This Boy’s Life; In Pharaoh’s Army), the novel Old School, and his work editing anthologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography emphasizes Wolff’s range as author and editor; one can assess his career by both the quality across multiple forms and his influence in curating contemporary short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition by major literary awards and honors
rubrics_metrics.description: “Wolff was the recipient of numerous awards, notably the 1985 PEN/Faulkner Award... He also won three O. Henry Awards... In 2015 he received the National Medal of Arts.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards and honors are presented as external validation of achievement; presence/absence of such recognition is an implicit metric of critical standing in evaluations.
